interpretation: The pinned public PoC was served and its module graph executed on the applet. The page logged only Attempt lines, and no Stage 1 trigger, alert, crash, reboot, or hang occurred in any of the four short modes. This is not a clean negative for CVE-2023-28205: the approved single-run protocol was not followed, each mode was reloaded after 16-58 s, and the highest attempt count is unknown. It does show that the PoC's module graph loads and the loop runs, but it does not establish whether the build is patched or whether a longer single run would trigger the UAF.
limitations: Protocol deviation: four page loads in four modes instead of one bounded page load; the heap and PoC state were reset at each reload.
Each mode ran only 16-58 seconds; the highest Attempt count was not recorded, so the PoC may not have run long enough to reach Stage 1.
The page's localStorage log was not exported; the Stage 1 result rests on the owner's Load logs view.
No crash dump or fault address was produced, so the result cannot distinguish a patched build from PoC incompatibility.
The exact WebKit patch level remains unknown, and Nintendo may have backported the MarkedVector fix.
A browser compromise would be applet-level only and would not reach Atmosphère without a separate kernel or boot-stage chain.
